question: to the Commission Fredis Beleris (PPE) Subject:

The ongoing crisis in the Middle East has led to instability and spikes in oil prices. This directly affects the European fishing sector, as it is highly dependent on fuel for the operation of fleets. However, countries such as Greece, which have a large number of fishing communities operating on a large scale at sea, are made to bear the brunt of this impact. For many fishers, and small-scale fisheries in particular, fuel costs already represented one of the biggest operating expenses. The recent price spikes could lead to further economic restriction, reduced fishing activity and additional economic pressure on coastal and island communities. With this in mind, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What data does it use to assess the impact of recent oil price increases on the viability of the European fishing fleet?
Is it considering the possibility of activating exceptional European support measures for the fishing sector – reinforcing national initiatives?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) The data used to assess the impact of recent oil price increases on the viability of the European fishing fleet are the scientific economic data formally submitted by Member States under the Data Collection Framework, analysed by the Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries (STECF). These data are also complemented by real-time marine diesel prices and market evidence collected by the European Market Observatory for Fisheries and Aquaculture products (EUMOFA). The Commission is aware that the situation in the Middle East has dire implications for the EU, including the EU fisheries and aquaculture sector. The Commission is closely monitoring the market situation of the sector since the inception of the crisis. Noting that a demonstrated and substantiated causal link between the exceptional situation in the Middle East and the significant disruption has been established, the Commission triggered the compensation mechanism provided under Article 26(2) of the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) Regulation with the adoption of the Commission Implementing Decision on 16 April 20261. Member States will be able to make this support immediately available to the sectors under their national EMFAF programmes, in line with the established EU rules. This exceptional EU support at EU level can reinforce national initiatives, including the use of State aid under the temporary crisis framework, adopted on 29 April 20262.
